newsitem.title: INDIA: India's United Front ready to choose new premier.
newsitem.headline: India's United Front ready to choose new premier.

text.p: India's ousted United Front coalition said on Friday it was on the verge of choosing a new prime minister after the Congress party lifted a roadblock to the formation of a centre-left government.
United Front officials said they expected the 15-party alliance to select a successor to caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda by Saturday at the latest.
"We hope to complete the exercise soon, latest by this night or tomorrow morning," United Front spokesman Jaipal Reddy told reporters after a meeting of alliance leaders chaired by Deve Gowda.
Deve Gowda's 10-month-old government fell on April 11 after losing a vote of confidence in parliament.
Congress, which triggered the downfall by withdrawing its crucial support, later said it would support a new government led by the United Front provided the alliance replaced Deve Gowda as leader.
But left-wing parties in the United Front refused to choose a new leader unless Congress president Sitaram Kesri withdrew a March 31 letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma staking a claim to power.
That threat helped to delay the choice of a new prime minister and raised the prospect of having to resort to mid-term polls to resolve the impasse.
Neither the United Front nor Congress want snap elections as opinion surveys show a vote would benefit the right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Moving to break the logjam, Kesri wrote to the president on Friday, offering to support a new United Front government provided the alliance replaced Deve Gowda.
Although the Congress chief told Sharma his March 31 claim to power would remain if Deve Gowda was not replaced, United Front leaders said Kesri's letter was enough to end the impasse.
"The reaction of the United Front was unanimous to the effect that any doubts about support of the Congress were laid to rest by the latest letter," Reddy said.
Reddy said Kesri's letter had satisfied leftist leaders. "That purpose has been served," he said.

The United Front cancelled a meeting of its decision-making Steering Committee set for 9:30 p.m. (1600 GMT) on Friday, but said the panel could meet at any time on Friday or Saturday to choose a leader, officials said.
Informal meetings among leaders to try to narrow a long list of contenders for the top job would continue on Friday.
The United Front brushed off suggestions that Congress had stopped short of withdrawing its claim to form a government.
"At a certain stage we need to trust," Reddy said. "I don't think the Congress has any idea of going back on its accord."
A United Front leader said: "Mr Kesri's letter falls short of grace, but it is tantamount to total withdrawal of the claim to power."
Nagging differences with Congress, political infighting and the death of a political boss prevented the United Front from meeting its own timetable and choosing a new leader on Thursday.

Regional parties were backing G.K. Moopanar, a former Congress member who defected last year to form a party in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, to be the new premier. But members of Deve Gowda's Janata Dal were reluctant to relinquish power.
